title: E-commerce platform
oneLiner: A hosted storefront whose sandbox checkout moves an order to PAID through a signed Stripe webhook, with stock decided under concurrency.

live.firstAction: Pay with the sandbox card 4242 4242 4242 4242 and watch the order move to PAID.
limits: The free instance sleeps after 15 minutes idle and takes about a minute to wake.
Payments run in Stripe test mode with the 4242 card; no money moves.
The catalogue is seeded: 30 products, 4 categories and 22 brands.
The four shots follow the visitor path — catalogue, product, cart and checkout — so the admin console is not in the set.

shots.alt: Store home page: the featured Technics SL-1200 MK5 panel with a currently-sold-out notice and a photograph of the turntable, above a New this month row of four from-priced tiles under the label Eight recent additions.
Sennheiser HD 598 product page: a headphone photograph on the left and a buy box with the 199.00 price, the Beige variant, In stock, quantity 1 and one Add to cart action on the right.
Cart with two lines at quantity 1 — Sennheiser HD 598 and Kestrel Pocket DAC — line totals, a server-computed 218.00 summary, free shipping and one Continue to checkout action.
Checkout with the Stripe Payment Element mounted: card, Pay By Bank, Bancontact, MB WAY, Satispay and EPS options, a Pay 218.00 action, and the recalculated order summary beside it.

measured.label: Hosted sandbox payment
measured.value: order KST-2610-53808809 PAID · 14900 cents · replay 200 duplicate
measured.method: node scripts/live-payment-proof.mjs against the hosted store with Stripe test keys; order and webhook detail in docs/PROOF.md

measured.label: Checkout concurrency on stock 5
measured.method: npx vitest run tests/integration/checkout.oversell.test.ts against PostgreSQL 16; transcript in docs/proof/concurrency-run.txt

measured.label: Checkout load, 50 virtual users
measured.value: p95 4.58 s · 250 checkout requests · 248 orders · 2 P2028
measured.method: k6 run load/checkout.js, 50 virtual users x 5 iterations against a production next start; summary in docs/load/checkout.md

measured.label: Verification gate
measured.method: npm run verify (eslint, tsc, vitest, prisma migrate diff, Playwright)

invariants.claim: A forged price in the checkout body cannot change the charge
One order per (userId, idempotencyKey) under concurrent double submit
20 concurrent checkouts on stock 5 create exactly 5 orders and stock never goes negative
An amount mismatch becomes REFUND_REQUIRED, never PAID
A replayed Stripe webhook is a 200 no-op
Expired reservations release stock and cancel the order

limits: The live checkout is one Stripe test-mode order; the load numbers come from a local build.
A checkout serialises on the variant row; concurrent buyers queue behind the conditional UPDATE.
No partial refunds, tax engine, shipping rates or email; refunds are all-or-nothing.
